messages.subject: For Mathilde Hellenes | Sustainability, Public Affairs & Circular-Economy Leadership | Executive Proposal
messages.body:
Dear Ms. Hellenes,

I am writing from Guyana, where I serve as Liaison Director, Social Responsibility at AGM Inc., part of Zijin Mining Group. My work spans sustainability, government relations, regulatory coordination, corporate affairs, stakeholder strategy and executive issue management inside a major regulated industrial operation.

TOMRA's global circular-economy mission and its work across recycling, collection, food and mining strongly align with the problems I manage today: converting sustainability ambitions into credible operating action, working across public institutions and industry stakeholders, and ensuring external commitments are supported by evidence and accountable ownership.

I prepared a TOMRA-specific Strategic Value Creation Proposal rather than sending a conventional CV alone. It outlines where I would add value across sustainability strategy, public affairs, stakeholder intelligence, circular-economy policy and responsible growth. My three-page Executive CV forms the final section.

I am open to relocation to Norway and employer-supported work authorization. My strongest fit would be a Director, Head or senior leadership mandate across Sustainability, Public Affairs, External Affairs, Government Relations, Strategic Partnerships, Responsible Business or emerging-market growth.

I would value a short confidential conversation. If Nicolai Prytz, Anika Jovik or another senior leader owns the most relevant mandate, I would be grateful if you would route the proposal internally.

Kind regards,
Ragunauth Ramsaroop
Liaison Director, Social Responsibility
AGM Inc. | Zijin Mining Group
ragunauthramsaroop@icloud.com
ragunauthramsaroop.com

strategic_brief.title: Strategic Value Creation Proposal: Sustainability, Public Affairs and Circular-Economy Growth
strategic_brief.executive_summary: TOMRA's purpose is closely linked to resource efficiency, circularity and climate action across more than 100 markets. Achieving that mission at scale requires more than technology. It requires regulatory awareness, public-policy engagement, disciplined stakeholder strategy and strong evidence behind sustainability claims. I bring director-level experience from a multinational mining operation where government relations, regulatory coordination, ESG, renewable-energy deployment and stakeholder commitments are integrated into daily operating decisions. My contribution would be to help connect TOMRA's sustainability and circular-economy ambition with institutional intelligence, market-facing execution and accountable stakeholder governance, particularly in emerging resource economies and regulated industrial sectors.
strategic_brief.company_context: TOMRA is headquartered in Asker, Norway and operates globally across collection, recycling and food sorting, with additional relevance to mining and material recovery. Its sustainability platform explicitly links the business to climate action, sustainable cities, responsible consumption and resource productivity. TOMRA also operates in markets where regulation is a major growth driver, including deposit return systems, extended producer responsibility, recycling standards and circular-economy policy. The company's 2026 strategy leadership structure places strategy, brand, communications and marketing within the executive team, while Group Sustainability has dedicated vice-presidential leadership. This creates a strong opportunity to connect sustainability expertise, public affairs, market intelligence and stakeholder execution into one disciplined approach to responsible growth across jurisdictions.

opportunities.title: Circular-economy policy intelligence
opportunities.rationale: TOMRA's addressable markets are strongly influenced by regulation, producer-responsibility systems, recycling mandates and public policy. Commercial opportunities are easier to anticipate when policy developments, institutional priorities and stakeholder positions are translated into business implications early.
opportunities.how_i_can_help: I would build executive-level policy and stakeholder intelligence that maps regulatory developments, decision-makers, industry positions and market-readiness signals to commercial priorities and strategic actions.

opportunities.title: Sustainability commitment governance
opportunities.rationale: A global sustainability platform depends on consistent ownership and evidence across business units and geographies. Strong governance reduces the gap between published ambitions and operating execution while improving assurance readiness and external credibility.
opportunities.how_i_can_help: I would strengthen commitment ownership, source evidence, escalation and review routines by applying operating experience from ESG, carbon-data governance and renewable-energy implementation in a regulated industrial environment.

opportunities.title: Emerging-market stakeholder strategy
opportunities.rationale: Circular-economy systems require cooperation among governments, regulators, municipalities, producers, investors and communities. In fast-growing markets, institutional capacity and stakeholder alignment often determine whether technically strong solutions move from concept to implementation.
opportunities.how_i_can_help: I would support market development with government engagement, stakeholder mapping, institutional partnership strategy and disciplined follow-through, drawing on direct experience in Guyana's rapidly expanding resource economy.

opportunities.title: Mining and resource-sector integration
opportunities.rationale: TOMRA's technology and sustainability proposition has particular relevance to mining and resource industries seeking higher efficiency, lower waste and stronger ESG performance. Commercial value increases when technology is positioned within the broader regulatory and social context of mine operations.
opportunities.how_i_can_help: I would help connect TOMRA's resource-efficiency proposition to mining-sector decision-makers, sustainability priorities, government expectations and site-level operating realities across selected international markets.

days_0_30: Map priority markets where circular-economy policy, stakeholder alignment and industrial sustainability create near-term strategic opportunity.
Review current sustainability and market-development interfaces for gaps in ownership or institutional intelligence.
days_31_60: Develop a pilot policy and stakeholder-intelligence framework linked to commercial and sustainability priorities.
Create market-specific engagement maps for selected resource and circular-economy opportunities.
days_61_90: Test the framework against live policy or customer opportunities and convert insights into executive actions.
Introduce a concise dashboard covering material policy changes, stakeholder positions, commitments and decision needs.
days_91_180: Scale the strongest methods across selected markets and business units.
Measure impact through opportunity conversion, stakeholder outcomes, assurance readiness and reduced execution friction.

potential_impact: Earlier identification of policy-led growth opportunities across circular-economy markets.
Stronger integration of sustainability commitments with accountable business execution.
Improved government and stakeholder positioning in emerging markets.
Additional strategic pathways connecting TOMRA's technology with mining and resource-sector sustainability priorities.
background_relevance: Director-level experience spanning sustainability, government relations, regulatory coordination, corporate affairs, social performance and executive advisory inside a multinational mining company.
Senior engagement with institutions responsible for mining, environment, energy, labour, standards, taxation, trade and investment, with cross-functional operating follow-through.
Experience supporting renewable-energy deployment and carbon-data governance, including source ownership, evidence traceability and stakeholder coordination.
Direct knowledge of mining and emerging-market operating conditions where sustainability, policy and commercial execution intersect.
